capabilities.statement: Explain what generative AI is and is not

benchmarks.label: Digital skills
benchmarks.graduateStatement: Graduates use the digital tools and technologies the subject relies on.
benchmarks.studentStatement: You can use the digital tools your subject depends on.

genericOutcomes.title: Concept map of a digital tool's capabilities and limits
genericOutcomes.learningOutcome: The student can explain what a generative AI tool can and cannot reliably do, distinguishing genuine capability from assumption.

genericOutcomes.title: Briefing explaining a digital tool's capabilities to colleagues
genericOutcomes.learningOutcome: The student can brief others on what a digital tool can be trusted to do and what checks they should still carry out before relying on it.

tierReading.practice: Applies the critical-use workflow of AI literacy to the critical friend, carries out supervised research and enquiry, works with data and sources, and communicates findings to different audiences.

tierReading.identity: Works ethically and increasingly independently, treating practitioner identity as still forming rather than fixed, shaped by decisions on their own learning and by how diversity, sustainability and professional practice bear on AI literacy.

tierReading.practice: Designs and critiques misconduct risks across methods, evaluates GenAI outputs critically throughout, and applies knowledge to current and complex problems with some originality.
tierReading.knowledge: Critiques the misconduct risks of AI literacy, its GenAI outputs and their bearing on current thinking, and sees where understanding runs out.
tierReading.identity: A reflexive practitioner who critiques how their own costs shape their benefits, weighs what this means for wider debate and for audiences acting on it, and treats their professional identity as still evolving through that scrutiny.
